method.selection_policy: LLM-selected market-relevant items from news_digest.json; preserves source metadata and excludes noise.

framework.Equities: Broad equity/risk sentiment; market-moving mega-cap/AI allowed; low-signal single-stock noise excluded.
framework.Commodities: Physical commodity futures framework; supply disruption/demand strength positive; supply increase/demand weakness negative.
framework.FX: USD-centric basket; non-USD currency strength positive; USD/DXY strength negative.
framework.Rates: Bond-price framework; yields up/selloff/higher-for-longer negative; yields down/bond rally/cooler inflation positive.

Equities.title: Equities: Pullback as Oil and yields rebound – Danske Bank
Equities.summary: Danske Bank’s Danske Research Team notes that global equities paused and are set to open lower as Oil prices and yields move higher following renewed US-Iran tensions.
Equities.reason: Direct equity-market risk-off signal: rising oil and higher yields tied to US‑Iran tensions push broad equities lower. High relevance because it describes a market-wide pause driven by macro/geopolitical flows rather than single-stock noise.

Equities.title: Chip stocks race towards biggest gains since dotcom era on AI demand
Equities.summary: Philadelphia Semiconductor Index rides Big Tech’s data centre spending spree to 75% gains in 2026
Equities.reason: Strong, market‑leading narrative: AI-driven chip/memory rally is the dominant structural equity theme and is driving large sector/market flows. High direction and relevance due to broad implications for technology leadership and index performance.

Equities.title: Foreign investors buy Japanese stocks for eighth week on AI rally
Equities.reason: Tangible flow evidence of the AI-led risk‑on theme: continued foreign buying in Japan reinforces the cross-border nature of the chip/AI rally. Relevance moderate-high as it confirms persistent inflows into equities tied to AI.

Equities.title: Asian stock markets claw back some early losses, Middle East crisis remains major concern
Equities.summary: Stock markets in Asia have recovered a majority of their early losses, but are still significantly down as the exchange of attacks between the United States (US) and Iran has escalated the Middle East crisis.
Equities.reason: Regional equity action shows short‑term volatility from Middle East hostilities: partial recovery but overall risk remains. Relevant as it captures market sensitivity to geopolitical newsflow and the uneven regional impact on equities.

Equities.title: Salesforce beats on earnings and revenue but full-year guidance comes in light
Equities.summary: Salesforce has been hammered by investors on concern that artificial intelligence models and services will disrupt some traditional software products.
Equities.reason: Company earnings that weaken confidence in software sector durability amid AI disruption create negative spillovers for cyclicality and sentiment across growth stocks. Material single‑company event with sectoral transmission, hence moderate relevance.

Equities.title: Salesforce's beat fails to convince the market that software can survive AI
Equities.summary: Salesforce is doing everything it can to signal to the market that this year's sell-off is unwarranted.
Equities.reason: Reinforces skepticism about incumbents in software amid AI transition. Lower relevance than broad macro pieces but important for sector positioning and near‑term investor sentiment.

Equities.title: AI boom outweighs Iran war pain, Korean central bank chief says
Equities.summary: Shin Hyun-song at first policymaking meeting projects boost to GDP on chip demand and surging stocks
Equities.reason: Official acknowledgement that AI/chip demand is driving GDP and equity strength offsets geopolitical headwinds — supports the dominant, pro‑equity AI narrative. Moderate relevance as it provides macro validation of the AI leadership theme.

Rates.title: US Dollar: Data focus and Fed expectations – Commerzbank
Rates.summary: Commerzbank’s Michael Pfister notes that if negotiations with Iran fail to progress, markets will turn to a heavy slate of US data, including the second estimate of first-quarter GDP and key PCE inflation readings.
Rates.reason: Explicitly flags markets shifting focus to major US data and Fed expectations — increases likelihood of hawkish Fed repricing if data prints hot, putting upside pressure on yields. Moderate relevance as it frames near-term drivers for rates.

Rates.title: Energy inflation has been more persistent than expected, Fed's Goolsbee tells CNBC
Rates.summary: While oil prices have recently fallen on news that a peace deal between the U.S. and Iran could come, prices are still significantly higher than before the war.
Rates.reason: Fed official noting persistent energy-driven inflation is a clear hawkish signal for monetary policy and raises the risk of higher-for-longer rates — negative for bond prices. Relevance moderate given direct inflation transmission.

Rates.title: US core PCE inflation set to edge up in April as markets price in Fed rate hike by year-end
Rates.summary: The United States (US) Bureau of Economic Analysis (BEA) will publish the Personal Consumption Expenditures (PCE) Price Index data for April on Thursday at 12:30 GMT.
Rates.reason: Core PCE is the Fed's preferred inflation gauge; an expected uptick directly bolsters market pricing for additional/extended tightening and pushes yields higher. High relevance because it's a key calendar data point for policy.

Rates.title: Fed’s Kashkari tells CNBC that inflation fight takes priority as labor market is 'in decent shape'
Rates.summary: The Minneapolis Fed President warned that persistently high inflation risks becoming embedded in consumer expectations, potentially forcing tougher policy action later.
Rates.reason: Senior Fed official emphasizing priority of fighting inflation increases the odds of continued or tighter policy, which is downward for bond prices/higher for yields. High relevance given speaker status and explicit policy intent.

Rates.title: Treasuries Resume Decline as US Strikes Push Oil Prices Higher
Rates.reason: Headline links geopolitical shock → oil spike → higher inflation expectations and a renewed selloff in Treasuries. Direct market-moving narrative for rates, hence sizable negative impact on bond prices.

Rates.title: US Bonds’ Return to Pre-War Calm Fuels Bets It’ll Be Short-Lived
Rates.reason: Discusses market positioning and the likelihood that a calm in bond markets is temporary — signals caution that yields may re-price higher again. Relevant to positioning/risk sentiment in rates.

Rates.title: Minutes of the Federal Open Market Committee, April 28-29, 2026
Rates.summary: Minutes of the Federal Open Market Committee, April 28-29, 2026
Rates.reason: FOMC minutes are primary source on officials' views; if they show concern about inflation or tolerance for tighter policy, that pushes yields higher. High relevance to policy-driven rate moves.

Rates.title: Kevin Warsh takes oath of office as chairman and a member of the Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System, and the Federal Open Market Committee unanimously selects Warsh as its chairman
Rates.summary: Kevin Warsh takes oath of office as chairman and a member of the Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System, and the Federal Open Market Committee unanimously selects Warsh as its chairman
Rates.reason: Change in Fed leadership is material for the policy outlook and market positioning. Markets will re-evaluate rate path and the statement raises uncertainty with a bias toward reassessing tightening plans — meaningful relevance to rates.

Rates.title: Mortgage refinance demand drops 18% as rates hit highest level since August
Rates.summary: Mortgage rates rose to the highest level in nine months, hitting refinance demand hardest. Homebuyers also pulled back but were still more active than last year.
Rates.reason: Concrete evidence that market interest rates have risen enough to disrupt mortgage activity — reinforces the narrative of higher-for-longer rates and real-economy transmission. Moderate relevance to retail interest-rate effects.

Rates.title: Brent: Crude breaks lower on US-Iran optimism – MUFG
Rates.summary: MUFG’s Lloyd Chan reports that Brent has fallen below earlier May lows, with prices dropping to around $94 per barrel. He attributes the move to growing optimism over a potential US‑Iran deal, though he stresses that uncertainty over an imminent breakthrough r
Rates.reason: Lower oil on peace optimism reduces near-term inflation risk, which is supportive for bond prices (yields lower). Relevant as a commodity-to-rates transmission but smaller than direct Fed/inflation signals.

Rates.title: Investors rush to buy TIPS ETFs to beat inflation. They could end up losing.
Rates.reason: Flows into inflation-protected securities indicate elevated inflation concern and can affect real-yield dynamics; signals investor positioning that can influence nominal and real rates. Relevance limited to demand/positioning nuance.

Rates.title: America’s hegemonic glory is under threat
Rates.summary: Along with excessive ‘guns and butter’ spending, that risk means long-term Treasuries are expensive
Rates.reason: Argues structural fiscal and geopolitical factors make long-term Treasuries expensive — implies upward pressure on long-term yields. Relevant to long-end rates and valuation discussion, but less immediate than policy/data releases.

FX.title: Euro: Risk-off pressure persists against US Dollar – Danske Bank
FX.summary: Danske Research Team notes that risk sentiment has deteriorated after fresh United States (US) strikes on Iran, pushing EUR/USD below 1.16. The team highlights that higher Oil prices and yields are weighing on broader risk assets.
FX.reason: Clear FX-native piece tying EUR/USD weakness to geopolitics (US strikes on Iran), oil and yields. Dominant USD-strength / risk-off narrative; high relevance given immediate market impact on major cross.

FX.title: Forex Today: US Dollar rises on escalating tensions in Middle East, eyes on inflation data
FX.summary: Here is what you need to know on Thursday, May 28:
FX.reason: Direct summary stating USD appreciation driven by Middle East escalation — large, market-moving FX signal. High relevance reflecting broad USD-flow impact ahead of macro data.

FX.title: ECB: Tightening bias with cuts pencilled for 2027 – ABN AMRO
FX.summary: ABN AMRO analysts note the European Central Bank (ECB) Governing Council has adopted a tightening bias and is expected to raise the deposit rate to 2.50% with hikes in June and July. Higher long-term inflation expectations support this stance.
FX.reason: ECB tightening bias is a structural support for EUR vs USD via rate-differential channel. Relevant but partially offset by stronger immediate geopolitical USD flows, so medium relevance.

FX.title: US Dollar Index: Range-bound trade persists on Iran peace hopes – DBS
FX.summary: DBS Group Research economist Philip Wee notes that the US Dollar Index (DXY) is consolidating in a tight range as markets price optimism over a potential US-Iran peace deal and reopening of the Strait of Hormuz.
FX.reason: Provides a counter-signal to the USD-strength narrative (peace hopes capping DXY). Included at modest relevance as it tempers but does not overturn the dominant risk-off USD bid.

FX.title: Japanese Yen: Downtrend intact against US Dollar with 159.95 in focus – UOB
FX.summary: UOB’s Quek Ser Leang and Lee Sue Ann report USD/JPY closed at 159.51, its second straight daily gain, and see scope for further upside. Intraday, they expect a test above 159.70, though 159.95 is unlikely to be reached yet.
FX.reason: JPY weakness vs USD close to key levels (near 160) reinforces USD-strength and intervention-watch narrative; high relevance for G10 FX flows and risk positioning.

FX.title: Japan Intervention Data Eyed as Yen Hovers Near 160 Per Dollar
FX.reason: Market attention on potential FX intervention is highly relevant for JPY and cross-market liquidity. While signalling USD strength, the intervention overhang could limit further moves — important for positioning.

FX.title: Swiss Franc softens on renewed US-Iran tensions, SNB intervention stance
FX.summary: The USD/CHF pair gains momentum to around 0.7895 during the early European trading hours on Thursday. Renewed tensions in the Middle East boost the US Dollar (USD) against the Swiss Franc (CHF).
FX.reason: CHF softening due to Middle East tensions is an FX-native safe-haven / USD-strength read. Relevant as it shows broad USD bid across safe-haven and major currencies.

FX.title: New Zealand Dollar loses traction as US–Iran tensions overshadow hawkish RBNZ policy outlook
FX.summary: The NZD/USD pair attracts some sellers to around 0.5885 during the early European trading hours on Thursday. The New Zealand Dollar (NZD) softens against the US Dollar (USD) as a fresh exchange of airstrikes between the United States (US) and Iran dented hopes
FX.reason: Emerging G10 / commodity-linked currency selling into a USD safety bid — reinforces the cross-market USD-dominant narrative, medium relevance given NZD's smaller market impact.

FX.title: USD/CAD Price Forecast: Extends rally to 1.3870, fresh high since April 13 on firmer USD
FX.summary: The USD/CAD pair is seen building on the previous day's breakout momentum through the 1.3810-1.3815 confluence hurdle and gaining positive traction for the third straight day on Thursday.
FX.reason: USD/CAD rally underscores broad USD strength; relevance also tied to commodity (oil) and Canada-specific flows but still a clear USD-dominant FX signal.

FX.title: Australian Dollar refreshes weekly low vs JPY on reduced RBA hike bets, intervention fears
FX.summary: The AUD/JPY cross extends the previous day's retracement slide from the 114.35 area, or a nearly two-week high, and attracts some follow-through selling for the second consecutive day on Thursday.
FX.reason: Cross-market move driven by RBA hike bets and intervention concern — FX-native but more cross/technical in nature; limited relevance to USD-basket except as a risk-off proxy.

FX.title: British Pound recovers against US Dollar; outlook remains weak due to Iran worries
FX.summary: The British Pound claws back half of its early losses and rebounds to near 1.3400 against the US Dollar (USD) during the European trading session on Thursday from the intraday low of 1.3367. The recovery move in the GBP/USD pair appears to be short-lived as Mi
FX.reason: Short-lived GBP rebound vs USD noted, but overall outlook remains GBP-weaker on Iran tensions. Included at modest relevance as it illustrates intra-day currency dynamics against the dominant USD bid.

FX.title: (BOJ Review) Developments in and Characteristics of Japan's FX Market: An Analysis Based on the 2025 BIS Triennial Central Bank Survey
FX.reason: BOJ research paper is FX-market material but is background/structural rather than time-sensitive. Low relevance for immediate directional scoring; included as contextual source.

Commodities.title: Oil jumps 3% after Iran says it targeted U.S. airbase following fresh American strikes
Commodities.summary: Oil prices rose on Thursday after fresh U.S. strikes in Iran renewed concerns over disruptions to commercial shipping through the Strait of Hormuz.
Commodities.reason: Direct, market-moving geopolitical escalation in the Middle East (US-Iran strikes) raises immediate risk-premium for oil via potential Strait of Hormuz disruption. High relevance to near-term crude price direction and market volatility.

Commodities.title: Oil: Geopolitics weigh on prices – Rabobank
Commodities.summary: Rabobank’s Global Strategist Michael Every notes that Oil prices remain below $100 even as geopolitical risks escalate in the Middle East. Every highlights US-Iran tensions, threats over the Strait of Hormuz, and ongoing military actions.
Commodities.reason: Analyst note reinforcing the dominant geopolitics-driven bullish narrative for oil, but with a tempered view (prices still below $100). Reinforces risk-premium upside for crude with moderate-high relevance.

Commodities.title: Oil Retreats on Hopes for Hormuz Opening
Commodities.reason: Counter-signal: reports of hopes or signs of the Strait of Hormuz reopening would reduce the immediate geopolitical risk-premium and weigh on oil. Lower relevance vs. direct strike reports.

Commodities.title: Gold Holds Losses as US-Iran Impasse Keeps Inflation Risk High
Commodities.reason: Headline indicates gold is not rallying despite heightened geopolitical/inflation risk—likely driven by a stronger USD or profit-taking. Net near-term negative price impulse for gold in current headlines.

Commodities.title: Gold seems vulnerable as break below $4,400/200-day SMA comes into play amid firmer USD
Commodities.summary: Gold (XAU/USD) maintains its heavily offered tone heading into the European session and currently trades just above a two-month low, touched earlier this Thursday.
Commodities.reason: Technical break and firmer USD driving gold lower in the near term. High-frequency price action and USD strength are dominant drivers for bullion here, giving this a clear bearish tilt.

Commodities.title: Hong Kong to Get Edge in Asia Gold-Hub Push With Clearing System
Commodities.reason: Structural market development that should support Asia gold market liquidity and physical flows over the medium term—mildly bullish for demand/market depth but lower immediate price impact.

Commodities.title: Silver Price Forecast: XAG/USD falls below $72.50 on US strikes in Iran, bearish technical signals
Commodities.summary: Silver price (XAG/USD) tumbles to around $72.30, the lowest since May 6, during the early European trading hours on Thursday. The precious metal faces some selling pressure amid renewed tensions between the US and Iran.
Commodities.reason: Silver is showing marked technical weakness and is trading down amid the same geopolitical shock that is moving oil—suggests risk-off flows and USD/technical pressure dominating, bearish for silver near term.

Commodities.title: Silver could fall further after latest slump, analysts say as they warn of demand destruction
Commodities.summary: Silver's rally of over 140% last year is deterring buyers in various industries and its elevated price levels are beginning to weigh on demand, UBS said.
Commodities.reason: Analyst warnings of demand destruction at elevated silver prices add a structural bearish element to the near-to-medium term price outlook, compounding technical/flow-driven weakness.

Commodities.title: Most planned natural gas pipeline capacity additions in 2026 and 2027 originate in Texas
Commodities.summary: Developers plan to bring approximately 44.9 billion cubic feet per day (Bcf/d) of new pipeline capacity online in the United States in 2026 and 2027, according to our latest Natural Gas Pipeline Projects Tracker. Approximately 70% (31.6 Bcf/d) of this new capa
Commodities.reason: Large planned pipeline additions increase takeaway capacity and supply flexibility in the US, exerting downward pressure on regional gas basis and price risk for natural gas into 2026-27.

Commodities.title: Data center server energy use grows across the commercial building stock
Commodities.summary: In the Annual Energy Outlook 2026 (AEO2026), our long-term outlook, we project electricity consumed by data center servers will increase across the commercial building stock, increasing more in standalone data centers than in all other data center rooms combin
Commodities.reason: Rising data-center electricity demand is a longer-term bullish demand signal for power and therefore for fuels used in generation (natural gas, to some extent coal). Lower immediate price impact but supportive structurally.

Commodities.title: Coal remains competitive for power generation in the central United States
Commodities.summary: In the first four months of 2026, electricity, natural gas, and coal prices suggested continued favorable economics for coal generation in MISO. The dark spread of coal, the difference between the fuel costs for coal-fired generation and the wholesale electric
Commodities.reason: EIA finding that coal is economically competitive in parts of the US supports continued coal burn and near-term demand for the commodity, a modestly bullish fundamental signal for coal markets.

Crypto.title: BlackRock's bitcoin ETF sheds $528 million, the second-largest daily outflow on record
Crypto.reason: Large institutional ETF outflows directly reduce aggregated BTC demand — significant negative for market liquidity and price sentiment.

Crypto.title: Bitcoin drops below $73,000 as U.S. strikes on Iran spark $1 billion liquidations
Crypto.reason: Geopolitical shock triggered large forced liquidations and a sharp intra-day BTC decline — high-impact, risk-off price event for crypto markets.

Crypto.title: Bitcoin gauge tracking selling pressure moves into 'high-risk' zone as ETF demand slumps
Crypto.reason: On-chain/ETF accumulation metrics flipping to outflows indicate elevated selling pressure and weaker structural demand for BTC.

Crypto.title: Bitcoin could be heading much lower, fund manager warns as $150 billion Treasury operation nears
Crypto.reason: Large upcoming Treasury issuance could drain USD liquidity and tighten funding conditions — downside risk for leveraged crypto positions and risk assets.

Crypto.title: Diverging trends: Ether slides below $2,000 while futures open interest hits record high of 16 million ETH
Crypto.reason: ETH price weakness coupled with record futures OI implies elevated leverage and liquidation risk — negative for near-term Ether volatility and price.

Crypto.title: U.S. CFTC files request to erase Gemini settlement that it no longer considers fair
Crypto.reason: Regulatory reversal/relitigation increases legal uncertainty for exchanges and custodians — negative for institutional participation and risk pricing.

Crypto.title: Major crypto exchanges increase transfer scrutiny with HTX over UK sanctions
Crypto.reason: Heightened counterparty and compliance scrutiny constrains exchange flows and could reduce liquidity in affected corridors — modestly negative operationally.

Crypto.title: Mastercard secures New York BitLicense to support stablecoin and digital payment infrastructure
Crypto.reason: Major payments network gaining BitLicense supports stablecoin/payment rails adoption — positive for on‑chain payments and institutional acceptance.

Crypto.title: Block kicks off Cash App’s phased stablecoin roll out to its nearly 60 million users
Crypto.reason: Wide consumer distribution of a stablecoin via Cash App materially expands on‑ramps and transactional use cases — constructive for liquidity and network effects.

Crypto.title: DTCC plans to bring tokenized assets to Stellar in latest Wall Street blockchain push
Crypto.reason: DTCC moving tokenized asset infrastructure to a public chain is a meaningful institutional vote of confidence for tokenization and on‑chain settlement.

Crypto.title: Crypto’s biggest exchanges back push for token disclosure standards as industry courts institutional capital
Crypto.reason: Coordinated disclosure standards reduce informational and regulatory frictions, increasing appeal to institutional investors — positive for capital inflows.

Crypto.title: BIS project finds tokenization could make cross-border payments faster, safer
Crypto.reason: BIS endorsement of tokenization tech supports regulatory and central‑bank interest in on‑chain payment rails — constructive long-term infrastructure signal.

Crypto.title: Crypto IPOs could create massive $1 trillion market amid tokenization wave, Jefferies says
Crypto.reason: Sellside bullish estimate on tokenized IPO market highlights potential upside from institutional product development, but remains forward‑looking and speculative.

Crypto.title: Google engineer insider-traded search results on Polymarket, Feds allege
Crypto.reason: Alleged insider trading on prediction markets undermines trust and could spur regulatory scrutiny of decentralized market platforms — modest negative reputational impact.
